text:
The Blues are the most honest team in the league right now. They are 7-7-2, with 49 goals for and 50 against, 49.6 expected for and 52.5 expected against, and 16 points against 16.6 deserved by their chances. Whatever you think of St. Louis, the numbers agree with you.

Their week summed it up. Down 4-1 late in the third in New Jersey, they clawed back to tie it 4-4, with Philip Broberg and Dalibor Dvorsky scoring two quick goals to finish the comeback, and then the Devils won it after regulation. That is a point taken from nowhere and a point left on the table in the same night.

Thomas, Dylan Holloway and Jimmy Snuggerud have played 156 minutes together and won 53% of the chances, the most stable unit on the roster. The Jonatan Berggren, Connor McMichael and Mason McTavish line drives harder, at 3.47 expected goals per 60. On the back end, Broberg and Adam Jiricek have been the better pair by a distance, 57% of the expected goals to the Cam Fowler and Brandon Carlo pair's 51%. Justin Barron has eight points in 10 games against 3.6 expected; enjoy it, but don't bank it.

Our simulations project 87 points and a 34% playoff chance. To beat that, this team has to stop being average at something.
headline: A .500 team that plays like one
